newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mount Nelson reverts to rand rates.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mount Nelson reverts to rand rates.

text.p: South Africa's premier hotel, Orient Express' Mount Nelson, on Tuesday succumbed to pressure to revert to rand-based room rates but warned that this could lead to higher rates.

Citing the instability of the rand and the need to protect its considerable capital investments in its African Collection stable of hotels, Orient Express started quoting U.S. dollar rates for bookings at the Mount Nelson in January this year.
Pre-bookings for its luxury sister hotel, The Westcliff in Johannesburg due to open in October, have also been quoted in dollars.

African Collection managing director Nick Sewar said in a statement that although the rand's weakness had been a cause of concern, a dollar-based pricing structure had brought about a different set of problems.
"These were chiefly in the invoicing, tour packaging and administration areas," he said.
"The situation was further complicated by the continual fluctuations in the rand value."
After representations from a wide number of interested parties, it had now been decided to revert back to rand-based rates for both hotels with immediate effect.
Seewar said that the group would now have to consider other strategies to protect the company's investments in the region.
"We cannot afford further devaluation of the rand and would have to adjust our rates in line with any further major decrease in the value of the South African currency," he said.
UK-based Orient Express Hotels is a subsidiary of Sea Containers Ltd and is spending more than $30 million on expanding and upgrading its operations in southern Africa.
